issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution implementation define Stock.take(String) to return an int, but the template repository's Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This return-type mismatch is structural: students following the UML or the solution will expect an int (e.g., -1 on failure) and may write code that checks for -1, which will not compile against the template signature. Conversely, using the template's boolean semantics will conflict with the specified behavior in the problem statement and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.take(String) method match the UML and solution by changing its return type from boolean to int and adjust its implementation to return -1 on failure and the remaining quantity on success (or otherwise follow the documented contract). This aligns the template with the problem statement and solution and prevents compilation/behavior confusion.
